reading: Each isolated cell becomes the centre of a 3x3 ornament (2 at centre, 1 on the edge cells, 3 on the diagonal corners); then a full row and full column of 1 is drawn through each centre over background cells only.
verb: stamp ornament and draw cross lines
why: Every marker gets the same 3x3 unit centred on it; lines of 1 run from each centre to all four borders along its row and column, painting only background (other ornaments' 3s stay). Equivalent: draw full lines first, then stamp on top.
invariants: background cells off the lines and ornaments

reading: Groups of 4-cells are partial plus shapes; the plus is completed by turning its remaining 5-cells into 2.

new_rows.name: plus_gap
new_rows.datalog:
pl(Y, X, Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C).
pl(Y, X, Y2, X) :- px(Y, X, C), off(DY, DX), DX = 0, Y2 = Y + DY, px(Y2, X, C2).
pl(Y, X, Y, X2) :- px(Y, X, C), off(DY, DX), DY = 0, X2 = X + DX, px(Y, X2, C2).
f4(O) :- obj(O, Y, X), px(Y, X, 4).
cand(O, Y, X) :- f4(O), obj(O, Y2, X2), pl(Y, X, Y2, X2).
miss(O, Y, X) :- cand(O, Y, X), obj(O, Y2, X2), !pl(Y, X, Y2, X2).
dirty(Y, X) :- pl(Y, X, Y2, X2), px(Y2, X2, 0).
centre4(Y, X) :- cand(O, Y, X), !miss(O, Y, X), !dirty(Y, X).
plus_gap(Y2, X2) :- centre4(Y, X), pl(Y, X, Y2, X2), px(Y2, X2, 5).

why: For each 8-connected component of 4s there is exactly one in-grid plus (centre + 4 orthogonal neighbours) containing all its cells whose other cells are all 5 (no 0); exactly those 5s become 2 (key 5->2).

reading: Every square object (square bounding box with its whole box outline filled, hollow or solid) gets eight 2-marks: the cells just outside each corner, continuing its top/bottom rows and left/right columns.

new_rows.name: sq_corner_marks
new_rows.datalog:
ylo(O, min(Y)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
yhi(O, max(Y)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
xlo(O, min(X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
xhi(O, max(X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
box(O, A, B, C, D) :- ylo(O, A), yhi(O, B), xlo(O, C), xhi(O, D).
sq(O) :- box(O, A, B, C, D), S = B - A, S = D - C, S > 0.
gap(O) :- box(O, A, B, C, D), px(A, X, K), X >= C, X <= D, !obj(O, A, X).
gap(O) :- box(O, A, B, C, D), px(B, X, K), X >= C, X <= D, !obj(O, B, X).
gap(O) :- box(O, A, B, C, D), px(Y, C, K), Y >= A, Y <= B, !obj(O, Y, C).
gap(O) :- box(O, A, B, C, D), px(Y, D, K), Y >= A, Y <= B, !obj(O, Y, D).
good(O) :- sq(O), !gap(O).
sq_corner_marks(Y, X) :- good(O), box(O, A, B, C, D), Y = A - 1, X = C, px(Y, X, K).
sq_corner_marks(Y, X) :- good(O), box(O, A, B, C, D), Y = A - 1, X = D, px(Y, X, K).
sq_corner_marks(Y, X) :- good(O), box(O, A, B, C, D), Y = B + 1, X = C, px(Y, X, K).
sq_corner_marks(Y, X) :- good(O), box(O, A, B, C, D), Y = B + 1, X = D, px(Y, X, K).
sq_corner_marks(Y, X) :- good(O), box(O, A, B, C, D), Y = A, X = C - 1, px(Y, X, K).
sq_corner_marks(Y, X) :- good(O), box(O, A, B, C, D), Y = B, X = C - 1, px(Y, X, K).
sq_corner_marks(Y, X) :- good(O), box(O, A, B, C, D), Y = A, X = D + 1, px(Y, X, K).
sq_corner_marks(Y, X) :- good(O), box(O, A, B, C, D), Y = B, X = D + 1, px(Y, X, K).

why: Only objects whose box is square (side >= 2) and whose box border is fully occupied get marks; diagonal pairs, lines and non-square rectangles get none. Marks are colour 2 on background.

reading: The single grey (5) shape is partitioned into 2x2 squares, coloured 8, and straight 1x3 bars, coloured 2.

slots.subject: the one 5-coloured object
slots.pieces: 2x2 square -> colour 8; 3-cell straight bar (horizontal or vertical) -> colour 2
slots.constraint: the pieces tile the shape exactly with no overlap

why: Every 5-cell is covered by exactly one piece; output differs from input only in the shape's colours.

reading: One large panel shows a 3x3 pattern drawn at 2x scale in a colour; in every small 3x3 panel of the separator grid whose 1-cells contain that pattern, those cells are recoloured to the pattern colour.

slots.key_pattern: the coloured shape inside the 6x6 panel, downscaled by 2 to a 3x3 mask
slots.panels: the 3x3 cells cut by the 4-coloured separator lines
slots.rule: if every mask position in a panel is 1, recolour those positions to the colour

why: Only 1-cells at mask positions in fully matching panels change; all separators, 0s and the large panel stay.

reading: Each closed one-cell-wide outline has its corner cells recoloured: convex corners become 4, concave corners become 2.

new_rows.name: concave
new_rows.datalog:
hmax(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
wmax(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
out(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 0), Y = 0.
out(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 0), X = 0.
out(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 0), hmax(M), Y = M.
out(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 0), wmax(M), X = M.
out(Y2, X2) :- out(Y, X), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, px(Y2, X2, 0).
hn(Y, X, DX) :- cell(Y, X, C), off(DY, DX), DY = 0, X2 = X + DX, cell(Y, X2, C2).
vn(Y, X, DY) :- cell(Y, X, C), off(DY, DX), DX = 0, Y2 = Y + DY, cell(Y2, X, C2).
concave(Y, X) :- hn(Y, X, DX), vn(Y, X, DY), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, out(Y2, X2).

new_rows.name: convex
new_rows.datalog:
hmax(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
wmax(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
out(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 0), Y = 0.
out(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 0), X = 0.
out(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 0), hmax(M), Y = M.
out(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 0), wmax(M), X = M.
out(Y2, X2) :- out(Y, X), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, px(Y2, X2, 0).
hn(Y, X, DX) :- cell(Y, X, C), off(DY, DX), DY = 0, X2 = X + DX, cell(Y, X2, C2).
vn(Y, X, DY) :- cell(Y, X, C), off(DY, DX), DX = 0, Y2 = Y + DY, cell(Y2, X, C2).
concave(Y, X) :- hn(Y, X, DX), vn(Y, X, DY), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, out(Y2, X2).
corner(Y, X) :- hn(Y, X, DX), vn(Y, X, DY).
convex(Y, X) :- corner(Y, X), !concave(Y, X).

why: A corner is an outline cell with one horizontal and one vertical outline neighbour; it is concave if the diagonal cell between those two neighbours is background connected to the grid border, else convex. Convex -> 4, concave -> 2; straight cells keep their colour.

reading: The 3x3 input has one uniform row or column; the 9x9 output places copies of the input in the matching row or column of 3x3 blocks, other blocks empty.
why: Block (i,j) holds the input iff i is the uniform row index (row case) or j is the uniform column index (column case); otherwise 0.

reading: Between a top line and a bottom line of different colours, each object slides vertically toward the line of its own colour until it touches that line.
why: Each object keeps its shape and column and ends in contact with the full border line of its colour (top or bottom); the two lines do not move. Note: in pair 0 the 3-tall 8 bar at column 15 appears as a 5-tall bar ending on the bottom line, which a rigid move does not produce.

reading: From each 5 in the bottom row a vertical line grows upward to the top border; every cell takes the colour of the nearest non-background cell at or below it in that column (the line changes colour each time it hits a cell).

new_rows.name: base5
new_rows.datalog:
hmax(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
base5(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, 5), hmax(M), Y = M.

why: Only columns with a 5 in the bottom row change; the line runs upward only, to the top border, and its colour switches to each hit cell's colour from there up.

reading: The 3x9 grid is three 3x3 blocks; each block's 5-pattern is classified and the whole block is filled with that pattern's colour.

slots.lookup: top row full -> 6; hollow ring (all but centre) -> 3; bottom row full -> 1; anti-diagonal -> 9; centre only -> 4
slots.output: each block entirely filled with its looked-up colour

why: Every output block is uniform and its colour depends only on the shape of the 5s in the same input block (same shape, same colour across pairs).
